sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax
sections.html:
One office in Shelby handles both valuation and collection: Cleveland County Tax Administration, inside the county administration building at 311 East Marion Street. Call 704-484-4843. Doors open weekdays, eight to five. Each fall the office mails and collects more than 60,000 tax notices for a county with 15 municipalities. Its website offers a record lookup, an online payment search, an address change request and a tax estimator.

The county has about 103,325 residents and 45,667 housing units. Homeowners occupy 70.9% of occupied homes, the median home value for 2020 to 2024 is $200,000, and owners with a mortgage pay a median of $1,257 monthly.

Cleveland reappraises land and buildings every four years, twice as often as the statute requires. Its current valuation date is January 1, 2025. Appraisers work from aerial and street photography, recent sales, land records, and details such as zoning, soil class and improvements, as the revaluation page explains. That is the information behind your value.

Until the next revaluation, the tax value on your parcel stays tied to that January 1, 2025 date.

The County Manager's recommended 2026-2027 budget keeps the county rate at 40.5 cents per $100 of valuation. With a public school rate and a fire tax rate added, the combined figure is 61.5 cents per $100.

Rates in the recommended 2026-2027 budget
Rate componentCents per $100
County property tax40.5 cents
Public school tax14 cents
Fire tax7 cents
Total61.5 cents

Check final figures, and any city or town rate, with the tax office. The school, fire and municipal rates that hit your bill depend on your parcel's location.

Four routes exist: a written appeal filed online, one sent by mail or email, or an in-person meeting. A phone call does not count as an appeal.

  • Online: the appeal form is on the county tax site, and each parcel needs its own.
  • Mail: a photocopy of the form goes to the Cleveland County Tax Assessor, P.O. Box 370, Shelby, NC 28151.
  • Email: send it to tax.assessor@clevelandcountync.gov.
  • In person: complete the request form that came with your notice, then phone 704-484-4911 to book a time.

Expect a mailed answer in eight weeks or longer. A review can end with the same value, a lower one or a higher one. Only two arguments count: the value is far above its likely selling price, or it was appraised unfairly against similar properties. Arguing about how big the jump was, citing an insurance value, or pleading hardship will not work.

Still unhappy after the informal review? Write to the Board of Equalization and Review to request a hearing before the board adjourns; the county announces that date on its site and in the local paper. Beyond the board sits the Property Tax Commission, and you have 30 days from the day the board mails its decision to go there.

sections.h2: Does a higher appraisal mean a higher bill?
sections.html:
Not always. The bill is tax value times rate, and every taxing jurisdiction picks its own rate, so after a revaluation some bills climb, others drop and a few barely move.

Appraisers can act on value alone. Concerns about services or affordability belong with the elected boards that set the rates. Before you appeal, open the county's assessment records map and turn on the Improved Sales and Vacant Sales layers, which the county suggests for finding recent comparable sales near your parcel. Vehicles, trailers and boats are valued every year, while land and buildings are valued only at a countywide revaluation.

The tax office website includes an online payment search and a record lookup, so you can see what is owed on a parcel before you list it. An address change request keeps notices from going to the wrong place after a move, and the tax estimator offers a rough preview of a bill. Tax Administration answers questions at 704-484-4843.

Sellers should check the balance early. The closing agent can only pay what the collector reports, and an old year turning up at the table is the kind of surprise to avoid.

The county tax assessor takes applications for three state programs. Applications usually close June 1, and only one program can be used at a time.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: $25,000 or half of appraised value, whichever is greater, is taken off what is taxed. For 2026 the household income ceiling is $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000 of appraised value is exempt, and the state form applies no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: your bill is held to 4 percent of income, or 5 percent if income sits between the limit and $58,200 in 2026. It takes five years of owning and living in the home, plus a fresh application each year.

Tax put off under the circuit breaker for the last three years is due when the home changes hands. A sale therefore ends the deferral, and the sum is added to your closing statement. Farm and forest land can also qualify for a present-use deferral, taxed at use value with the difference carried on the books.

September 1 is the due date; January 5 is the last day before interest starts. Bills are figured and mailed in July after the rate-setting boards act.

Interest begins at 2 percent on January 6, and three-fourths of 1 percent more is added every month from February 1. The lien attaches to the parcel as of the listing date, so any unpaid year stays with the house.

For unpaid tax, the county can foreclose; its tax foreclosure page walks through it. Auctions happen in the Commissioners' Room, second floor, with 5 percent down from the high bidder. A challenger has to beat the bid by $750 or 5 percent, whichever is more, filing in person at the courthouse, and every upset bid opens a new ten-day period. The owner can still redeem until confirmation by the court.

Request a payoff figure from the collector. The settlement agent pays it out of your proceeds, so the buyer takes on nothing. Any back years are paid off at closing, interest included.

For a parcel already in foreclosure, the liens are listed in the complaint in the clerk's file. Pull it at the courthouse, 100 Justice Place in Shelby, using the CV file number. If repairs or back taxes are making an ordinary sale difficult, our North Carolina page explains a cash option.

faqs.q: When must a Cleveland County bill be paid?
faqs.a: By September 1. Paying after January 5 adds 2 percent, then three-fourths of 1 percent for each month that follows, starting in February.

faqs.q: How do I challenge my Cleveland County appraisal?
faqs.a: File a written appeal online, by mail to P.O. Box 370, Shelby, or by email, or ask for an in-person appointment at 704-484-4911. Phone appeals are not accepted, and a mailed decision can take at least eight weeks.

faqs.q: Is Cleveland County on the standard eight-year cycle?
faqs.a: No. State law caps the gap at eight years, but the county revalues every four. Its latest revaluation took effect January 1, 2025.

faqs.q: By when must relief paperwork reach the county?
faqs.a: June 1 is the usual deadline for the tax year. The elderly or disabled exclusion, disabled veteran exclusion and circuit breaker are all filed with the county, not the Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: May I close on a sale while taxes are owed?
faqs.a: Yes. Get the balance from the collector and have it paid from your proceeds. If foreclosure has started, you can still redeem until the court confirms the sale.
